picks.title: Ollama brings free, local text-to-speech to your Mac with natural-sounding AI voices
picks.rationale: New release: Ollama added local text-to-speech on Mac using Gradium's small Phonon models. It is free, needs no subscription, and runs fully on-device.
picks.excerpt: Ollama now lets Mac users turn text into natural-sounding speech locally with Phonon, a family of small text-to-speech models from Gradium. No subscription required.

picks.title: Apple MacBook Pro M6 just unveiled with 30% faster graphics, 25% faster AI and up to 24 hours of battery life
picks.rationale: New hardware: Apple's M6 launch puts the new chip in the 14-inch MacBook Pro (and the iMac), claiming 25% faster AI performance. This one card covers the whole M6 launch cluster.
picks.excerpt: Apple's new 14-inch MacBook Pro moves to the M6 chip, which Apple says brings 30% faster graphics and 25% faster AI performance, plus up to 24 hours of battery life.

picks.title: [Hands-On] Comfort, Convenience, and More: A Day With Galaxy Buds On
picks.rationale: New product: Samsung's first clip-on, open-ear Galaxy Buds On launched in Korea with hands-free Gemini Live ('Hey Google, let's talk Live') and head-gesture call handling. This is the primary source for the launch.
picks.excerpt: Samsung's first clip-on open-ear Galaxy Buds On launch in Korea with hands-free Gemini Live ('Hey Google, let's talk Live'), head-gesture call handling and up to 9.5 hours of playback.

picks.title: Opera wants websites to run AI on your laptop instead of sending your data to the cloud
picks.rationale: New preview: Opera WebAI lets websites and extensions call AI models running locally on the user's computer, with per-site permissions. It is a new on-device AI platform for the browser.
picks.excerpt: Opera’s WebAI preview lets websites and extensions use AI models running locally on supported computers, avoiding cloud processing and separate subscriptions while leaving access under the user’s control through site-specific permissions.

picks.title: This old Nokia phone got an AI Upgrade it was never designed for
picks.rationale: New hack: a developer vibe-coded 'Claude S40', which lets a 2G Nokia 6300 talk to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok through a small Go server. It adds a reading mode and offline saving.
picks.excerpt: A Turkish developer vibe-coded 'Claude S40', an app that lets a 2G Nokia 6300 talk to Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini or Grok via a small Go server, with a reading mode and offline saving of responses.

dedup.note: Apple M6 cluster c3: kept the Tom's Guide MacBook Pro M6 piece. Dropped the Digital Trends iMac M6 card because it is the same launch event, and Digital Trends already has 2 picks. Its history_match (10-06 Gizmodo wireless GPU) is unrelated. Galaxy Buds On cluster c11: kept the Samsung Newsroom primary source. Dropped The Elec's launch story (same event) and the TechRadar 'enough open earbuds' opinion piece (commentary on the same launch). Their 10-17 Samsung language-support match is a different story. Dropped on other grounds: Gemini Live 'plus' redesign (9to5Google, minor UI tweak following the 10-26 Gemini redesign card, also dropped on 10-27); Android Authority Gemini Live visualizer sneak peek (unreleased teardown, same Gemini UI redesign thread); Android Authority Gemini remembered-items teardown (speculative APK, dropped 10-27); Intel Arc B580 XeStrata (single benchmark, dropped 10-27); INMO GO3 (flagged as sponsored on 10-26); Google Maps CarPlay Gemini (10-21, stale, and too close to the 10-21 blog.google Gemini-on-the-road card). No Apple Creator Studio item was considered, since it is reserved for movies. Cross-section: every pick was published after the 10-27 brief's collection cutoff (10-26 22:00 UTC), so none can be in published_urls.json from an earlier day. The orchestrator should still check for same-day 10-28 clashes, especially Ollama TTS with music and Apple M6 with movies or design. Diversity: 4 outlets (Digital Trends x2, Tom's Guide, Samsung Newsroom, Engadget).
